proof.argument: Every legal global injection restricts to an allowed context assignment and an injective next-symbol assignment in each native row. Dropping context equality, context/output agreement and cross-row agreement enlarges the feasible set. Independent row minima therefore sum to a lower bound for every globally consistent key. SPACE and BOS must remain fixed typed symbols; ordinary rows never map to them.

For fixed target context, cost is frequency_x times target_cost_t. Nonnegative frequencies descending paired with the lowest distinct target costs ascending minimize the rectangular injection sum by rearrangement; unused consonants receive zero-frequency rows. Add SPACE separately. Sorting conservatively rounded lower ticks and minimizing them remains a valid lower bound even if rounding changes the selected minimizer.

Construct integer inputs exactly. At precision60, correctly rounded Decimal.ln(integer) lies between its adjacent representable values; handle ln1=0 exactly. Positive ln2 endpoints and directed subtraction/division give bounds for ln(D)-ln(N) divided by ln2. Taking max(0,lower_difference) is sound for D>=N. Directed conversion to2^-32ticks and all later integer arithmetic preserve bounds. This assumes the documented Decimal correctly-rounded ln primitive, not an arbitrary host libm float.

For each native history, sequential Dirichlet-half probability has numerator product_x product_j(2j+1), denominator product_j(2j+K). Context totals suffice since within-context products commute. Histories reset by locus; counts do not reset. Upper cost uses upper log denominator-product minus lower log numerator-product. All events, including SPACE, use the same stream and K=m+1. BOS is history only; no EOS added.

Key log2(P(21,m)) and selector log2(6) lower bounds may be added. Identical common overhead cancels. A strictly positive integer lower margin over KT upper certifies no key beats that baseline in this fixed family. Finite-union claim requires every pack. Nonpositive bounds do not produce a key, certify model success or prove a useful tight approximation.
